What it leaves to you is everything around it: where the runtime lives,"},{"id":"p19s2","text":" how it gets upgraded, which port to use when one is taken, whether child processes survive the app,"},{"id":"p19s3","text":" where `DSH_HOME` points, and who restarts the server when it dies. This app owns all of that."},{"id":"p20s1","text":"## What it does"},{"id":"p21s1","text":"| **Dual-slot updates** | The runtime is installed by npm into `runtime/slot-a` or `slot-b`, with `c"},{"id":"p21s2","text":"urrent.json` naming the active one. An update installs into the idle slot, boots a probe server agai"},{"id":"p21s3","text":"nst it, and only moves the pointer once that self-test passes — a failed upgrade leaves the working "},{"id":"p21s4","text":"version untouched. The previous version stays in the other slot, and one menu item goes back to it —"},{"id":"p21s5","text":" no network, no reinstall. |
| **Update channels** | `dsh` publishes a new build to npm's `next` dis"},{"id":"p21s6","text":"t-tag first and moves `latest` later, so a version can be plainly released and still be invisible to"},{"id":"p21s7","text":" anyone tracking `latest`. Stable follows `latest`, Preview follows `next`, and the check reads both"},{"id":"p21s8","text":" tags in the one request it already makes — so being up to date on Stable can say that Preview holds"},{"id":"p21s9","text":" something newer, rather than leaving that as a puzzle. A channel that points *below* the installed "},{"id":"p21s10","text":"version offers the move down as what it is, and the self-test and the other slot apply to it exactly"},{"id":"p21s11","text":" as they do to an upgrade. |
| **App self-update** | The version here against the newest GitHub rele"},{"id":"p21s12","text":"ase, in two flavours. A **hot update**, when the new version only changes the shell (JavaScript and "},{"id":"p21s13","text":"markup): a few hundred KB into the data directory, live after a restart, with the installed app bund"},{"id":"p21s14","text":"le untouched — so its signature, and the privacy permissions macOS binds to it, survive. An **instal"},{"id":"p21s15","text":"ler update**, when Electron or the bundled runtime changed: the app downloads the installer and hand"},{"id":"p21s16","text":"s it to you. Checked once, quietly, after startup, and from the menu whenever you like. |
| **Proces"},{"id":"p21s17","text":"s ownership** | The server starts with the window on a random free port and loads once it answers HT"},{"id":"p21s18","text":"TP 200. It runs in its own process group (POSIX) or job tree (Windows), and the whole tree is termin"},{"id":"p21s19","text":"ated when the app quits — no orphans. |

Later starts only refresh the current `src/` an"},{"id":"p25s3","text":"d `assets/` trees and renew the ad-hoc signature. The menu bar, Dock and window therefore all say **"},{"id":"p25s4","text":"DeepSeek Harness** while still running the current source, without downloading Electron again. Use `"},{"id":"p25s5","text":"npm run start:electron` only when debugging the raw host; that command is expected to show **Electro"},{"id":"p25s6","text":"n** in the menu bar."},{"id":"p26s1","text":"[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p27s1","text":"## Known limitations"},{"id":"p28s1","text":"- `dsh` is at release-candidate stage. The contract this app depends on is deliberately minimal: `ds"},{"id":"p28s2","text":"h web --port N`, plus HTTP 200 at the root meaning ready. Check those two first when an upstream cha"},{"id":"p28s3","text":"nge breaks something.
- The local port is reachable by any process on the machine (`dsh` has no auth"},{"id":"p28s4","text":" token yet). A random port narrows the window; it does not close it.
- Conversations need `DEEPSEEK_"},{"id":"p28s5","text":"API_KEY`, set either in the `dsh` web UI settings or in the environment before launch.
- macOS build"},{"id":"p28s6","text":"s are ad-hoc signed and not notarized: the first launch needs approval under System Settings → Priva"},{"id":"p28s7","text":"cy & Security.
- macOS protected folders (Documents, Desktop, Downloads, external volumes) are walle"},{"id":"p28s8","text":"d off from the app: a plugin installed from a local path inside one of them fails to read with `EPER"},{"id":"p28s9","text":"M`. The plugin manager appends what to do about it. The grant is bound to the code signature, and an"},{"id":"p28s10","text":" ad-hoc signature changes with every reinstall, so it has to be given again after an update; install"},{"id":"p28s11","text":"ing from a zip puts the plugin in the app data directory and sidesteps the whole layer."}],"truncated":true}
